about: Bills coded to the alignment questions (public/questions.json): {question id: {bill id (congress-type-number, as in the bill index): [side index, why, optional {votes: [roll calls]}]}}. An optional {sponsor: false} leaves out the sponsorship of a measure its sponsor brought up only to vote it down (the 2019 Senate Green New Deal resolution). The votes list names the only roll calls (chamber, Congress and Voteview roll number) that count for a bill: for a bill number that was later reused as the vehicle for something else, or (an empty list) when a vote against the bill doesn't mean taking the other side. A key like "vote:H117-9" codes a roll call that belongs to no bill, such as an objection to a state's electoral votes: a Yea takes the coded side. A bill is coded only when it is clearly on one side of the question; procedural measures (rules for considering a bill), budget resolutions, large packages where the question is one provision among many (a law counts on the tax questions when tax changes are among its main purposes, as with the 2017 and 2025 tax laws, and the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act on corporate taxes), and bills that apply to a single territory are left out. Each was read from its titles and the Congressional Research Service's summary (scripts/question-bills.mjs lists the candidates).
